hypothesis: With the core's paths cut, the device's worst path is the transfer engine's request: the in-bounds tests for a load word or a store's byte enables are rebuilt in every cycle from t_CB and t_E with 64-bit adds, subtracts, a max/min and eight range compares, in front of the request's valid -- and the valid steers the core's memory mux and from there the memory's write enables. The bounds are constant for a whole transfer, so registering them leaves one 36-bit offset against registered constants; steering the request's fields by state instead of by which request is valid takes the late valids out of the address and enables. No cycle moves.
evidence_for_hypothesis: tnca_fpga_top post-synthesis, 6.667 ns target, after timing-004..007: u_txf/t_P3 -> u_mem WEA 7.197 ns / 38 levels (t_CB_reg -> u_mem WEA 6.998 ns in the build before: 17 CARRY8 of bounds arithmetic, then the request mux, the address and the memory's range check)

microarch.change: w0 = 8*t_unit - r_m (the unit's low word's offset from the box row start); load low/high word tests as w0 in (K1, K2) / (K1-8, K2-8) with K1 = -8 - t_CB, K2 = t_E - t_CB; store byte j as w0 in [max(0,-t_CB) - j, min(t_row_bytes, t_E - t_CB) - j); all bounds registered every cycle from t_CB/t_E/t_row_bytes, which S_TCHK sets and S_TMUL (at least one cycle) separates from the walk; mem_req_addr/tag/we/be/wdata selected by state (S_DLOAD/S_TRUN/S_SRUN/else), equal to the old selection whenever the request is valid

compatibility.cycles: unchanged: R2 cycle check over the 149 R37 O2 cases, and every core program
compatibility.numerics: the same predicates by algebra (each bound moved across its inequality; no operand near 2^63); t33 (672 window-lane checks of rank 1-5 loads, negative/misaligned/past-the-end coordinates, zero/NaN fill), t34 (400 memory-word checks of stores), t35 refusals, t17, r38-xpose-rtl
